notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Melee: Adventure mode no longer crashes in its first stage. The game crashed the first time a
block on the Mushroom Kingdom route was hit; the launcher now fixes that in the downloaded game
before each start, so a console that already has Melee gets the fix too.

Joy-Cons as two Wii Remotes: a new controller type in a Wii game's Controllers menu, for the
Joy-Cons. The right Joy-Con plays on its port and the left on the next one. Each stick is its
remote's d-pad, each Joy-Con's motion moves its own pointer, and every button can be remapped,
SL and SR included. Recenter is on the stick buttons. Motion and SL and SR need the Joy-Cons
detached.

Wii U motion: the GamePad's gyro works in Cemu. Handheld it follows the console, docked a
detached Joy-Con or Pro Controller. Motion controls and Motion source are in the game's
Controllers menu.

Stremio draws its pages on the GPU, so docked it answers a press about three times faster.
Selecting a text box in Stremio opens the keyboard, and in YouTube the Minus button opens it.
The basic keyboard has a symbols page (the #+= key). Stremio and YouTube have the Controller
row and Remap that PC games have, and Set hotkeys is gone from Ports and Apps.

Library views: each box takes its cover's shape, with bevelled edges, so covers shaped like a
game case no longer get grey bars in Cover flow. ZL and ZR jump to the previous and next
letter (or date, or play time, by the sort), and a tab with more than 20 games shows a letter
wheel as you jump. In the rolodex, Up brings the next game forward and Down goes back.

Settings opens as a list of its sections: pick one and the list slides aside, and Back returns
to the list.

Saves: PSP save folders and NDS saves are in Manage Files and on the web page, to download or
delete. The web page's Debug tab can take a screenshot of the console's screen.

Fixes: docked, YouTube answers presses right away and its sticks work. Opening the in-game menu
no longer resets a custom fan curve (it could send the fan to full speed). The screen no longer
turns itself off a few seconds after waking the console from deep sleep. An Xbox controller's
triggers reach Moonlight with their whole travel instead of only on or off.

Not tried yet: Joy-Con motion and SL and SR as Wii Remotes, Wii U motion in a game, a real Xbox
controller's triggers, and the deep sleep fix on a real wake (it was tested in a simulation).

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
